question: Does processing CFR action phases in storage preorder/reverse preorder preserve all bits and improve throughput?
scope: Only batch::run phases 1 and 3; terminals, id-indexed value rows, f64 recursion, EV/BR and artifact formats are unchanged.
decision: Local correctness acceptance passed. No performance acceptance or speed claim; integrator will measure AWS c6a.8xlarge at 16/32 threads.

source.newSource: Containing commit; measured code was uncommitted during verification.

environment.noise: Shared Windows development machine; alternating runs are informational only.

baseline.source: Provided main baseline; source revision not embedded in the binary and not independently recorded here.

memory.mapping: Vec<NodeId>, one u32 per action node
memory.capacitySlack: Additional spare Vec capacity; actual capacity was not instrumented. No per-pass allocation or sort is added.

verification.newRegressionTest: solver::batch::tests::storage_preorder_matches_recursive_bits_when_node_order_differs (passed debug and release; both players, prune/unpruned, zero/nonzero reaches, per-action CFV and full f32 regret/strategy sum bits)
verification.existingCoverage: Workspace and release suites retain vector_determinism, batch grouping/precision, and artifact/checkpoint tests.

reproduction.configGeneration: For each case read examples/hu-postflop/{case}.toml, append newline [solver] newline cfr_precision = "{precision}" newline, and write under E:/solvers-tmp/s5/.
reproduction.timingOrder: For f32 then i16: prechange, storage_order repeated three times, sequentially after compilation and correctness checks finished.
reproduction.bitComparison: Parse report nashConv as IEEE-754 f64; compare all 64 bits (big-endian hex) across three binaries and thread counts.

configs.content:
# Small HU river with explicit ranges and a one-BB bet; suitable for a quick solve.
schema = "solvers.nlh/v1"

[table]
players = 2
stack_bb = 5

[spot]
line = "BTN r2.5, BB c / BB x, BTN x / BB x, BTN x"
board = "Ks 7h 2d 3c 9s"

[ranges]
BTN = "AhAd,QhQd"
BB = "JhJd,ThTd"

[tree]
script = '''river { replace bet [1bb] }
river when !unopened { replace raise [a] }'''

# CFR arithmetic in [solver]: cfr_precision = "f32" (default) | "f64" (legacy bit-identical).
# Storage choices in [solver]: auto (default: f32 if it fits, otherwise i16-f32avg), f32, i16, i16-f32avg.
# DCFR defaults: alpha = 1.25, beta = 0.5, gamma = 4.
# Omitted pow4_reset: true for i16, false for auto/f32/i16-f32avg; explicit values take priority.
[solver.stop]
max_iterations = 16
check_every = 4
# Integer cadence stays fixed; default "auto" adapts with target, otherwise evaluates every 25.

[run]
threads = 1

[solver]
cfr_precision = "f32"

# Specification section 14: six-max BTN vs BB single-raised flop pot with cash rake.
# Lean GTO Wizard-style tree: one flop c-bet size, no donk bets, small raises then all-in.
# About 3.7 GiB of f32 storage; see the user guide for adding sizes and their memory cost.
schema = "solvers.nlh/v1"

[meta]
name = "6max NL50 BTN vs BB SRP Ks7h2d"

[table]
players = 6
stack_bb = 100

[economics]
kind = "cash"

[economics.rake]
rate = 0.05
cap_bb = 4

[spot]
line = "BTN r2.5, BB c"
board = "Ks 7h 2d"

[ranges]
BTN = "22+,A2s+,K2s+,Q5s+,J7s+,T7s+,97s+,86s+,75s+,65s,54s,A5o+,K9o+,Q9o+,J9o+,T9o"
BB = "99-22,AJs-A2s,KJs-K2s,Q4s+,J6s+,T6s+,96s+,85s+,74s+,64s+,53s+,43s,AJo-A2o,K8o+,Q9o+,J9o+,T8o+,98o"

[tree]
script = '''
flop {
  when donk { remove bet }
  replace bet [33]
  replace raise [50]
  when aggressions >= 2 { replace raise [a] }
}
turn {
  when donk { remove bet }
  replace bet [50]
  when cbet { replace bet [75] }
  replace raise [a]
  when spr > 3 { replace raise [50] }
}
river {
  replace bet [50, a]
  when in_position { replace bet [75, a] }
  replace raise [a]
}
'''
allin_threshold = 0.67

[solver.stop]
target = "0.1%pot"
# Default check_every = "auto" adapts evaluation intervals from 3 to 50 iterations.

[run]
max_time = "1h"

[solver]
cfr_precision = "f32"

retention.availability: Compact results and generated input contents are Git-backed in this file. Full raw JSON/log files and benchmark binaries are locally retained at the recorded Windows paths on the measurement date; not Git-backed or guaranteed available on another machine.

risks: Mapping increases resident tree metadata by 4 bytes/action plus Vec capacity slack and header.
Small river/turn configurations have only two combos per player; flop case, recursive bit regression, and existing suites add broader coverage.
Local medians are noisy and do not establish AWS 16/32-thread performance.
Optional storage-order EV/BR change deliberately not implemented, preserving a separately measurable scope.
